mainTopic: Unloading an animal on שבת without moving מוקצה, צער בעלי חיים, and whether using the 'sides' (צדדין) of an animal or tree is forbidden
overview: This passage finishes a question from the previous section: why isn't a person liable for making his animal carry a load on שבת? Even the opinion that gives מלקות for such a לאו learns from the extra word 'אתה' that a person is liable only for his own work, not his animal's. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה about reaching the outer courtyard. רב הונא rules that if the animal carries glass vessels, the owner may put cushions underneath, untie the ropes, and let the bags fall. The גמרא challenges this twice. First, why not simply lift the glass off, since the משנה allows taking movable vessels? Answer: רב הונא means a bloodletter's horns, which are מוקצה. Second, doesn't this make the cushion unusable (מבטל כלי מהיכנו)? Answer: we are dealing with small bundles.

steps.title: Even the view that gives lashes learns from the word 'You' that there is no liability for the animal's work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its explanation of why one is not liable for driving a loaded animal on שבת. It does this even according to the view that gives מלקות for this type of לאו. The extra word 'אתה' teaches that a person is liable only for his own work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who says we give lashes: let the Torah write only 'Do not do any work... and your animal.' Why do I need the word 'you'? To teach that he himself is liable, but for his animal's work he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation for why a person who drives his loaded animal on שבת is not punished. This one works even for the opinion that gives מלקות for such a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason given was that this לאו carries the warning for a death penalty, so it cannot bring מלקות. That reason does not work for the opinion that says one does get מלקות for such a לאו. So the גמרא points to the word 'אתה', which seems extra in the פסוק, and learns from it that liability applies only to work a person does himself, not work done by his animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') write
Why do I need it? (points to an extra word)

steps.confusionAlert: Driving the animal is still forbidden on שבת. The point here is only that there is no punishment (מלקות) for it. 'Not liable' is not the same as 'permitted.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why מחמר (driving a loaded animal) is an איסור without punishment. That background is what makes the later rules about unloading the animal necessary.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says they give lashes,
phrases.notes: This refers to lashes for a לאו that carries a warning of a court death penalty.

phrases.english: let the Torah write
'Do not do any work... and your animal,'
why do I need 'you'?
It is he who is liable,
but for his animal he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier. It offers a second reason for no liability that works even for the opinion that gives lashes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the reason that a death-penalty לאו cannot bring lashes, one might think a person gets מלקות for driving his animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'אתה' limits liability to a person's own work, so there is no liability for the animal's work.

steps.title: רב הונא: unloading glass vessels onto cushions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about reaching the outer courtyard. Then רב הונא rules that if the load is glass, the owner may lay cushions underneath, untie the ropes, and let the bags fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He reached the outer courtyard.' רב הונא said: If his animal was loaded with glass vessels, he brings pillows and blankets and puts them under it. Then he unties the ropes, and the sacks fall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about unloading the animal. רב הונא adds a practical rule for fragile loads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows untying the ropes so the sacks fall by themselves, which avoids directly moving מוקצה. But glass would shatter if it fell. So רב הונא allows softening the fall with cushions, which also prevents the animal from suffering under the load.

phrases.english: He reached the outer courtyard.
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of a line in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If his animal was loaded with glass vessels,
he brings pillows and blankets
and places them under it,
and unties the ropes
and the sacks fall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: practical unloading, based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a load of glass, he may place cushions under the animal, untie the ropes, and let the sacks fall onto them.

steps.title: Why not just lift the glass off, since the משנה allows it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the משנה, which allows taking off vessels that may be moved on שבת. Glass vessels are such vessels, so why the complicated cushion method?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: 'He takes off the vessels that may be moved on שבת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's ruling, using the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary glass vessels are not מוקצה and may be handled on שבת. So the owner could simply remove them by hand, and the cushion method seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (a challenge from a משנה)
Those that may be moved on שבת

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
He takes the vessels that may be moved on Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's cushion method for glass vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Glass vessels may be moved on שבת, so according to the משנה he should simply remove them by hand.

steps.title: רב הונא meant a bloodletter's horns, which are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא was not talking about ordinary glass. He meant a bloodletter's horns, which are useless for anything else and therefore מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא said this, he meant a bloodletter's horns, which are not fit for him to use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what kind of glass רב הונא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting horns are disgusting and have no other use, so they are מוקצה and may not be lifted by hand. That is why the indirect cushion method is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A bloodletter's horns (glass cups used for bloodletting)

phrases.english: When Rav Huna said it,
it was about a bloodletter's horns,
which are not fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רב הונא meant ordinary, movable glass.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant מוקצה glass, which cannot be lifted by hand.

steps.title: Doesn't this make the cushion unusable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Placing מוקצה items on the cushion makes the cushion itself forbidden to move, which is the problem of מבטל כלי מהיכנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is taking away a vessel's readiness for use!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the מוקצה horns rest on the cushion, the cushion can no longer be moved. חז״ל forbid putting a usable vessel into a situation that makes it forbidden to move.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking away a vessel's availability for use on שבת

phrases.english: But he is negating a vessel's preparedness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cushion becomes a base for מוקצה and can no longer be moved, which is forbidden as מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

steps.title: The case is small bundles
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we are dealing with small bundles, so the cushion does not become stuck as a base for מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about small bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the second challenge by limiting the case to small bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small bundles will not break if the cushions are later pulled out from under them. So the cushions can still be removed and are not permanently made unusable.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's cushion method applies to מוקצה glass (a bloodletter's horns), and only in small bundles. That way the cushions can still be removed, and there is no problem of מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

phrases.english: With small bundles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the cushion would be stuck under the מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Small bundles do not break, so the cushions can be withdrawn.

steps.title: A ברייתא says to just let the bags fall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: an animal loaded with טבל and glass. You untie the ropes and let the bags fall, even though they break. No cushions are mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If his animal was loaded with טבל and glass, he unties the ropes and the bags fall, even though they break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says to simply let the glass fall and break, and it says nothing about cushions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said you may put cushions under מוקצה glass to protect it. This ברייתא deals with מוקצה glass too, yet it says to let it break. That suggests cushions are not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
Produce not yet tithed, which is מוקצה on שבת

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If his animal was loaded
with untithed produce and glass —
he unties the ropes
and the bags fall,
even though they break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רב הונא's cushion ruling after the מבטל כלי מהיכנו issue was resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that cushions may be placed under מוקצה glass
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets מוקצה glass fall and break without cushions. This implies cushions are forbidden.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about raw glass passages
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about כולסא, raw chunks of glass that are meant to be broken and melted down anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about chunks of glass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about finished glass objects. It means raw lumps of glass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw glass passages will be broken and melted to make new vessels. Letting them break causes no real loss, so there is no reason to allow cushions. רב הונא's case was a bloodletter's glass horns, which do get ruined if they break.

keyTerms.meaning: Raw chunks of glass meant to be melted down

phrases.english: There, it is referring to chunks of glass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (different type of glass)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's glass is the same as רב הונא's glass, so cushions should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's glass is raw passages, so breaking them causes no loss. רב הונא's horns would be ruined if they broke, so they may get cushions.

steps.title: The wording supports the glass-passages reading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the glass next to טבל. Just as טבל is not usable now, the glass is also something not usable, like raw passages.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also precise, since it teaches the glass alongside טבל. Just as טבל is not fit for his use, here too the glass is not fit for his use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא's own wording supports the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing glass together with טבל suggests the two are similar. Both are things the owner cannot use right now. That fits raw glass passages, not finished glass vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (it supports this reading)
It is not fit for him to use

phrases.english: It is also precise,
since it teaches it similar to untithed produce.
Just as untithed produce is not fit for him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָכָא נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: so too here, it is not fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 8 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא refers to raw glass passages
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists glass next to טבל, which suggests both are unusable items.

steps.title: Why mention that they break?
steps.stepSummary: If the glass passages are meant to be broken anyway, why does the ברייתא say "even though they break"?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is meant by "even though they break"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the wording of the ברייתא. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "even though they break" makes it sound like there is a loss. If the passages are meant to be broken, that phrase seems pointless.

phrases.english: And what is meant by "even though they break"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברייתא's wording given the answer of step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא mentions breaking if there is no real loss

steps.title: A small loss is not a reason to permit
steps.stepSummary: Some small slivers of glass do get lost when the passages smash. The ברייתא teaches that חכמים did not worry about such a small loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that they were concerned even for a small loss. It teaches us that they were not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the phrase teaches something: a small loss does not justify cushions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When raw passages fall, a few slivers get lost. One might think חכמים would allow cushions even for that small loss. The ברייתא's wording teaches that they did not.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Cushions are allowed under מוקצה only when breaking would cause a real loss, like ruining glass horns. A small loss, like slivers lost from raw passages, is not enough.

phrases.english: You might have said
that they were concerned even for a small loss,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches that a small loss is not enough reason to allow cushions.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: push the grain off with your head
steps.stepSummary: If an animal carries a load of grain, the owner may put his head under it and push it to the side, and it falls on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: If his animal was loaded with a bundle of grain, he puts his head under it and moves it to the other side, and it falls by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another way to unload a מוקצה load on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving מוקצה in the normal way, with your hands, is forbidden. Pushing it with your head is an unusual way of moving it, and that is allowed. Once pushed to the side, the load slides off by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea about מוקצה: moving it in an unusual way, like with your head or body, is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
If his animal was loaded
with a bundle of grain —
he places his head under it,
and moves it to the other side,
and it falls by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling about unloading מוקצה from an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה load may be pushed off an animal with one's head, since that is an unusual way of moving it.

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל's donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל's donkey was loaded with honey. He refused to unload it until שבת ended, and after שבת the donkey died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל's donkey was loaded with honey, and he did not want to unload it until after שבת. After שבת it died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבן גמליאל. This story sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל was so strict that he left the load on until after שבת, and the donkey died from the strain. The story raises a question: why didn't he unload the honey?

phrases.english: The donkey of Rabban Gamliel
was loaded with honey
and he did not want to unload it
until the end of Shabbat;
at the end of Shabbat it died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story related to unloading an animal on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל did not unload his donkey's honey on שבת.

steps.title: But the משנה allows taking off usable items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says you may take off items that can be moved on שבת. Honey can be moved, so why didn't רבן גמליאל unload it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: He takes off the items that may be moved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey is normal food, so it is not מוקצה. The משנה allows taking such items off the animal. So רבן גמליאל should have unloaded it.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?
Items that may be moved on שבת

phrases.english: But didn't we learn
"He takes the items that may be moved"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's refusal to unload the honey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Honey can be moved on שבת, and the משנה allows unloading such items. So why leave it on?

steps.title: The honey had spoiled
steps.stepSummary: The honey had gone bad, so it was not usable and was מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it had spoiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the honey had spoiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spoiled honey is not edible, so it became מוקצה. The משנה's permission only covers items that may be moved, so this honey did not qualify.

phrases.english: When it had spoiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case (the honey was spoiled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The honey was normal food that may be moved, so he should have unloaded it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The honey was spoiled and מוקצה, so the משנה's permission did not apply.

steps.title: What is spoiled honey good for?
steps.stepSummary: If the honey was spoiled, why was רבן גמליאל carrying it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Spoiled honey, what is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why anyone would carry spoiled honey. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not haul useless goods. So the spoiled honey must have had some use, even if not as food.

phrases.english: Spoiled honey, what is it fit for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer of step 15.

steps.title: For camels' wounds
steps.stepSummary: Spoiled honey was used as a salve for camels' sores.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the wounds of camels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that spoiled honey is used to treat camels' wounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That is why רבן גמליאל was carrying it. It is not food, so on שבת it is מוקצה, and he could not unload it with his hands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל left the honey on because it was spoiled and מוקצה. Spoiled honey was carried because it was used to treat camels' wounds.

phrases.english: For the wounds of camels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Spoiled honey is used to treat camels' wounds.

steps.title: Why not just untie the ropes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבן גמליאל could have untied the ropes and let the bags fall off by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him untie the ropes, and the bags will fall!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל did not use a simple workaround: untie the ropes and let the bags drop on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the spoiled honey was מוקצה and could not be handled, untying ropes does not mean holding the honey directly. So there seems to be a permitted way to relieve the donkey. Why did he let it suffer?

phrases.english: Let him untie the ropes and the bags will fall!
phrases.notes: This is exactly what the משנה permits for מוקצה loads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the honey was מוקצה, but asks why he did not use the indirect method the משנה allows.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's decision to leave the load on the donkey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A permitted indirect method existed, so he had no reason to let the donkey suffer.

steps.title: The jugs would crack
steps.stepSummary: If the bags simply dropped, the jugs of honey would break.
steps.simpleTranslation: The jugs would crack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that dropping the bags would have smashed the jugs inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Untying is fine when the load is sacks of grain. Here the honey was in breakable jugs, so letting them fall would cause a loss of property.

keyTerms.meaning: jugs or flasks (here, holding the honey)

phrases.english: The jugs would crack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail about the case (breakable containers)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Untying the ropes was an easy, loss-free option.
steps.terutzMaskana: Untying would break the jugs and cause a loss.

steps.title: Why not put cushions underneath?
steps.stepSummary: Let him place cushions and blankets under the bags so the jugs land softly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him bring pillows and blankets and place them underneath them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another workaround: put soft cushions on the ground, then untie the ropes so the jugs fall safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to solve the breaking problem from Step 19. Cushions are not מוקצה, so moving them is allowed.

phrases.english: Let him bring pillows and blankets
and place them underneath them (the jugs)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer of Step 19 with a way to avoid breakage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that relieving the donkey would cause a loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cushions remove the breakage problem, so there is still a permitted method.

steps.title: The cushions would get dirty and become unusable
steps.stepSummary: The cushions would be soiled by the spoiled honey, and he would ruin a usable item on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would get dirty, and he would be removing a vessel from its readiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cushions would be ruined by the sticky honey, and that this itself is a problem on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the money lost, there is a שבת issue called מבטל כלי מהיכנו. Making a usable item unusable on שבת, for example by putting it under something מוקצה or getting it filthy, is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: taking an item out of its usable state on שבת (rabbinically forbidden)

phrases.english: They would get dirty,
phrases.notes: The honey was spoiled and messy.

phrases.english: and he would be removing a vessel from its readiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a שבת prohibition that blocks the workaround
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cushions are a permitted, harmless solution.
steps.terutzMaskana: Using cushions would ruin them and violate מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

steps.title: But the animal is suffering!
steps.stepSummary: Even with all these losses, isn't the donkey's suffering more important?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the suffering of living creatures!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: even if every option costs money or touches on a rabbinic rule, צער בעלי חיים should override that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If causing an animal pain is forbidden by the Torah, it should outweigh both a money loss and a rabbinic rule like מבטל כלי מהיכנו. So רבן גמליאל should have accepted the loss.

phrases.english: But there is the suffering of living creatures!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grants all the earlier answers but argues that animal suffering should outweigh them.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's choice to let the donkey suffer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צער בעלי חיים should override monetary loss and rabbinic concerns.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל holds that animal suffering is a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that צער בעלי חיים is only rabbinic, so it does not override these other concerns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: the suffering of living creatures is a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל holds the rule against causing animals pain is only מדרבנן, not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צער בעלי חיים is only rabbinic, it does not automatically beat the rabbinic rule of מבטל כלי מהיכנו or a monetary loss. That explains why he left the load on.

keyTerms.meaning: from rabbinic law, not from the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source in the debate over whether צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא or דרבנן. Many later authorities rule that it is from the Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: The donkey story ends with this answer: רבן גמליאל's behavior is explained by his view that צער בעלי חיים is only דרבנן.

phrases.english: He holds: the suffering of living creatures is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22 and closes the רבן גמליאל discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the opinion the actor holds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צער בעלי חיים is from the Torah and overrides everything else.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבן גמליאל it is only rabbinic, so it does not override the other concerns.

steps.title: רבה slides his son on a donkey's back
steps.stepSummary: אביי finds רבה sliding his son along a donkey's back on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי found רבה rubbing his son along the back of a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. This step sets up the case: רבה was playing with his son by sliding him on a donkey on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rabbinic rule against using animals on שבת, such as riding them. So this behavior looks like a problem, and the next step will raise it.

phrases.english: Abaye found Rabba
rubbing (sliding) his son
along the back of a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about using animals on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבה placed his son on a donkey on שבת.

steps.title: אביי objects: you are using an animal on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה for making use of an animal on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Master is making use of animals!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges his teacher: using an animal on שבת is forbidden by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים forbade riding or leaning on animals on שבת, so that a person will not cut a branch to drive the animal. Sliding a child on a donkey seems to fall under this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: master (a respectful way to address a teacher)

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Master is making use of animals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action described in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's action of putting his son on the donkey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using animals on שבת is rabbinically forbidden.

steps.title: Using the sides was never forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that he is only using the animal's sides, which the חכמים did not forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They are sides, and the Rabbis did not decree regarding sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the rabbinic ban covers only direct use of an animal, not its 'sides'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה draws a line. Riding or leaning on the animal itself is forbidden. Using something attached to the animal, or using its sides in an indirect way (צדדין), was never included in the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: sides (indirect use of an animal or tree)

phrases.english: He said to him: They are sides,
and regarding sides the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.confusionAlert: צדדין does not mean the child was not touching the donkey at all. It is the name for a kind of indirect use that the decree left out.
steps.triggerLanguage: צְדָדִין הֵן, וּצְדָדִין לָא גְּזַרוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of an animal on שבת is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Using the 'sides' is outside the decree.

steps.title: Proof from our משנה about untying the ropes
steps.stepSummary: רבה proves his view from our משנה, which allows untying the ropes. That seems to involve leaning on the animal's sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you say this? As we learned: One unties the ropes and the bags fall. Is it not about bags tied with straps, which involve the sides, and the Rabbis did not decree about sides?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a proof from our משנה. It permits untying the ropes, even though doing so means pressing against the donkey's sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bags were strapped tightly, untying them requires leaning on the animal's sides. The משנה still allows it. That suggests using the sides is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you say this? (asks for a source)
as we learned in a משנה
a kind of bag or strap attachment on a pack animal

phrases.english: From where do you say this?
As we learned: One unties the ropes and the bags fall.
Is it not when the bags are tied on with straps,
phrases.notes: Untying them requires pressing against the animal.

phrases.english: which counts as using the sides,
and regarding sides the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's answer in Step 26 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: Using an animal's sides is permitted on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: מתיר חבלים והשקין נופלין

steps.title: No, the bags were attached in a way that does not use the sides
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the משנה may be talking about bags attached loosely or with a simple rope, so no leaning is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is with a hooked attachment, where there are no sides. Alternatively, it is with a rope.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רבה's proof by reading the משנה as a case where you do not lean on the animal at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bags hang on a hook-type attachment or a simple rope, they can be released without pressing on the animal's sides. Then the משנה says nothing about whether צדדין are allowed, and רבה's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: a rope or simple tie (per the reference translation)

phrases.english: No, it is with a hooked attachment,
phrases.notes: Per the reference translation, a loose hook-type attachment.

phrases.english: where it does not involve the sides.
Alternatively, with a rope.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא — בְּאֵבֶר גְּווֹלְקֵי, דְּלָא הֲווֹ צְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבה's rule itself is not disproven here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה involves leaning on the sides, but it may describe an attachment that needs no leaning.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from a סוכה built on a tree
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a משנה: a סוכה with one wall on a tree is valid, but you may not enter it on יום טוב. That suggests using a tree's sides is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: Two walls by human hands and one on a tree is valid, but one may not go up to it on יום טוב. Is it not where he wedged it into the tree and covered with it, which is using the sides, and sides are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's rule with a משנה about a סוכה that leans on a tree. Entering it on יום טוב is forbidden, even though it seems to use only the tree's 'sides'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tree on שבת or יום טוב is forbidden by the same kind of decree as using an animal. If the beam was only wedged into the side of the tree and the סוכה is still forbidden, then צדדין are forbidden. That contradicts רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Two walls made by human hands, and one on a tree,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: it is valid, but one may not go up into it on יום טוב.
Is it not where he wedged it into the tree
[and put the covering on it], which is using the sides,
phrases.notes: Bracketed words appear in the text.

phrases.english: and sides are forbidden!

steps.confusionAlert: The סוכה is still כשרה for the מצוה. The problem is only about entering it on יום טוב.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: שְׁתַּיִם בִּידֵי אָדָם, וְאַחַת בְּאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבה's proof, אביי now brings a source that seems to disprove רבה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that צדדין are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוכה משנה forbids entering a סוכה that uses only the tree's sides, which implies צדדין are forbidden.

steps.title: The tree was bent and used as the roof support
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the forbidden סוכה is one where the tree was bent over and the סכך was put on it, so the tree itself is being used.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where he bent the tree over and put the roofing on top of it. In that case he is using the tree itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself against אביי's proof from the סוכה משנה. He explains that the משנה is not talking about the tree's sides at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that entering the סוכה is forbidden because it uses the tree's sides. רבה changes the picture: the tree was bent, and the roof rests directly on it. Entering would then mean using the tree itself, which everyone agrees is forbidden. So the משנה tells us nothing about sides.

keyTerms.meaning: The roof covering of a סוכה (סכך)

phrases.english: No, it is where he bent the tree over
and placed the roofing on top of it
so he is making use of the tree itself

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the סוכה משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוכה is forbidden because entering it uses the tree's sides
steps.terutzMaskana: The סוכה is forbidden because the roof rests on the bent tree itself

steps.title: The second half of the same משנה permits entering
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the end of the משנה permits a סוכה with one wall on a tree. If the tree were bent under the roof there too, it should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: three walls made by a person and one on a tree is valid, and you may enter it on יום טוב. If the tree was bent, why may you enter it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's new explanation by quoting the next case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every 'tree סוכה' in the משנה is a bent tree holding up the roof, then the last case should also be forbidden. Yet the משנה permits it. So רבה's 'bent tree' reading does not fit the whole משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end clause (of the משנה)
One may go up into it, i.e., enter and use it

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ בִּידֵי אָדָם וְאַחַת בְּאִילָן כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: three walls made by a person and one on a tree is valid,
and one may enter it on a Festival.
And if he bent the tree,
why may one enter it on a Festival?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's 'bent tree' explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the משנה is about a bent tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bent tree would make the סיפא forbidden too, but the סיפא permits entering

steps.title: The same question hits אביי's view too
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that אביי's question is just as hard for אביי. Even if צדדין are forbidden, the סיפא still permits entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what do you say instead, that sides are forbidden? In the end, the question stays: why may one enter it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה turns the question back on אביי. He shows that the סיפא is a problem for both views, so it cannot prove אביי right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צדדין are forbidden, a סוכה leaning on a tree should also be forbidden in the סיפא, yet it is permitted. So אביי's own view cannot explain the סיפא either. Both sides now need a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides of an object, using it indirectly

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on רבה. רבה is showing that אביי's question works against אביי too.

phrases.english: But rather, what? Sides are forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף אַמַּאי עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: In the end, why may one enter it on a Festival?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by showing it is equally hard for him
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that צדדין are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under אביי's view, the סיפא's permission is just as hard to explain

steps.title: The tree only serves as a wall
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a new explanation. The משנה is about a tree with spread-out branches that is itself used as a wall, not a tree that holds anything up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there it is talking about a tree with spread-out branches, where he made the tree itself into a mere wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a new way to read the whole משנה. The tree acts only as a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree is simply one of the walls; nothing leans on it. When it is a necessary wall, the סוכה relies on the tree, so entering is forbidden. When it is an extra fourth wall, the סוכה does not need it, so entering is permitted. Under this reading, the משנה is not about צדדין at all.

phrases.english: Rather: there it is with spread-out branches,
where the tree itself
he made into merely a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading after the 'bent tree' reading failed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a bent tree or about leaning on the tree's sides
steps.terutzMaskana: The tree is just a wall; the ruling depends on whether the סוכה needs that wall

steps.title: The משנה's rule supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the משנה's general rule supports the new reading: if the סוכה can stand without the tree, one may enter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches: This is the rule. Whenever the tree could be removed and the סוכה could still stand, one may enter it on יום טוב. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the משנה's own wording for רבה's new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule asks whether the סוכה could stand without the tree. That test makes sense if the tree is just a wall, possibly an extra one. So the wording fits the explanation that the tree serves only as a wall.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (it supports this)
Learn from this, it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The סוכה-on-a-tree משנה does not settle whether צדדין are forbidden. The tree there acts only as a wall, and the test is whether the סוכה can stand without it.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ יִנָּטֵל הָאִילָן
phrases.english: This is the rule: whenever, if the tree were removed,
it could still stand,
one may enter it on a Festival.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation in step 33
steps.raayaObject: The tree in the משנה serves only as a wall
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule: if the סוכה can stand without the tree, one may enter it

steps.title: Maybe this is an argument among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רבה and אביי matches an argument among תנאים about entering a סוכה built against a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a dispute of תנאים? One may not enter it on יום טוב. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: one may enter it on יום טוב. Isn't this what they argue about: one holds sides are forbidden, and the other holds they are permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: is the רבה–אביי argument already an older argument among תנאים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא records two opinions about a סוכה that leans on a tree. The גמרא suggests the forbidding opinion matches אביי, who forbids צדדין, and רבי מאיר matches רבה, who permits them.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is like a dispute of תנאים?

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
One may not enter it on a Festival.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
One may enter it on a Festival.
Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds sides are forbidden,
and the other master holds they are permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line: is the רבה–אביי argument a dispute among תנאים?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תנאים argue about צדדין, like רבה and אביי

steps.title: Everyone forbids sides; the argument is about sides of sides
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the suggestion. Both תנאים forbid צדדין; they argue only about צידי צדדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No. Everyone agrees sides are forbidden. Here they argue about the sides of the sides: one master holds the sides of the sides are forbidden, and the other holds the sides of the sides are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away the comparison to the תנאים. He says they are arguing about a more distant kind of use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the תנאים all forbid צדדין, which fits his own view. Their argument is about צידי צדדין: for example, a wall supported by a beam set into the tree, not leaning on the tree itself. רבי מאיר permits that more distant use, and the תנא קמא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sides of the sides, a more distant indirect use

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up צדדין (leaning directly on the tree's side) with צידי צדדין (leaning on something that is attached to the tree).
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, all the תנאים forbid צדדין. רבי מאיר permits only the more distant צידי צדדין.

phrases.english: Abaye said: No,
everyone agrees sides are forbidden,
and here they disagree about the sides of the sides:
one master holds the sides of the sides are forbidden,
and the other master holds the sides of the sides are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צְדָדִין אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that the תנאים argue about צדדין
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects matching the רבה–אביי argument to the תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנאים may agree that צדדין are forbidden and argue only about צידי צדדין

steps.title: רבא says the opinions are all-or-nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי's split. Whoever forbids צדדין also forbids צידי צדדין, and whoever permits צידי צדדין also permits צדדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The one who forbids using the sides also forbids using the sides of the sides. The one who permits using the sides of the sides also permits using the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading of the argument between the תנאים, in place of אביי's reading from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said both תנאים agree that צדדין are forbidden and argue only about צידי צדדין. רבא says no one holds a middle position. The תנאים argue about the whole idea: one side forbids both levels, and the other side permits both.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a third reading of the תנאים's argument

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (the one arguing with אביי from step 24 on) with רבא here. They are two different אמוראים with very similar names.
steps.whyThisMatters: In רבא's reading, one of the תנאים does permit צדדין. That means אביי's claim that everyone forbids צדדין is no longer certain.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The one who forbids using the sides
also forbids using the sides of the sides,
and the one who permits using the sides of the sides
also permits using the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading from אביי's in step 36 of how the תנאים argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument among the תנאים is all-or-nothing. Forbidding צדדין goes together with forbidding צידי צדדין, and permitting צידי צדדין goes together with permitting צדדין.

steps.title: רב משרשיא begins a challenge to רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא starts to raise an objection against רבא from a source that opens with the word נעץ. The source continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא raised an objection to רבא: If one stuck in…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבא. Only the opening word of the challenging source appears here, and the rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איתיביה tells us a formal challenge from an earlier source is coming against רבא's all-or-nothing view. We cannot know the exact attack until we see the full quote. Expect a source that seems to split צדדין from צידי צדדין.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (by quoting an earlier source)
An אמורא who challenges רבא here
He stuck in or drove in (an object)

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya raised an objection to Rava:
If one stuck in (drove in)…
phrases.notes: The quoted source is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבא's statement in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that no one holds a split position between צדדין and צידי צדדין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source, quoted in full on the next amud, will apparently show a ruling that does not fit an all-or-nothing view.
